name: Goblin Discothèque
flavor: A wild goblin party that you were not invited to.   Not that that's going to stop you, of course.

rooms.prompt: This nerdy looking goblin at the door is trying to tell you that you're not allowed to enter with your weapons and armor that you are clearly brandishing.

on_success.message: They don't even try to fight, and curls into a ball.  You feel a bit bad, but not bad enough to not take their lunch money before moving on.
They look the other way and you pass on through

rooms.prompt: That last fight really got you moving!  Something is off though... are the beats being played most ungroovy, or are you just not drunk enough for this shit?

actions.label: I am too sober for this

name: The Gnomish Bathhouse
flavor: A sweaty place, full of sweaty gnomes.  Woe to ye who enters here.

rooms.prompt:
You finally make it to the entrance of the bathhouse.  Looks like they've got a coat check here too but... that coat check guy looks familiar.

Too familiar.

Seems like they might recognize you too.  What do you do?

on_success.message: You slip right past him before they're able to put anything together.  Sucker.

on_fail.message: A hand on your shoulder stops you.  Uh oh.

on_success.message: You don't got no time for wimps like this guy.

rooms.prompt: As you enter the Bathhouse proper, you are immediately assaulted by what appears to be a selection of malfunctioning, yet still magical, bath accessories.

"YOU AGAIN?  OH HOW I HAVE WAITED FOR THIS MOMENT.  YOU MAY HAVE GOT ME FIRED FROM MY LAST JOB, BUT I HAVE BEEN TRAINING EVERY WAKING MOMENT FOR THE CHANCE THAT I GET MY REVENGE"

The Gnome...er.... Goblin's dorky, nasal voice is really starting to grate on your nerves.

"EN GARDE, MY NEMESIS."

Oh that is -it-.

The gnomes are gaining on you. Soaked, furious, and closing fast.

Up ahead: a beaded curtain, glowing red, reeking of sweat and leather. Or a crack in the pipes, just barely wide enough to squeeze through, that might lead outside.

No time to think. Pick one.

The pipe spits you out into damp darkness. Not outside, like you'd hoped.

The air is heavy and old, thick with rot and something fouler underneath. Stagnant water laps at your ankles, and you can just make out shapes beneath the surface. Bones, maybe. Or something that used to have them.

Whatever has been sleeping down here has been sleeping for a very long time. You get the distinct feeling you just woke it up.

You shove through the curtain into velvet and candlelight, pumping techno bleeding through the walls from somewhere unseen.

The walls are hung with things you don't want to look at too closely: leather straps, polished chains, hooks that definitely aren't for towels. The air is thick with candle wax, sweat, and something sweeter underneath.

Someone has been very busy in here. And they don't look happy to be interrupted.
As you remove the curtains to enter in what you think is the main room, it turns out you stumble into a private bath!

The Frustrated Witch lies slumped against the tub, wheezing. Behind her, the floating bath apparatus she'd been wrangling all fight is now completely unsupervised and spinning wildly out of control as they spray suds -everywhere-.

on_success.message: Between the two of you, you wrestle the apparatus back under control. She glares at you, snatching it back. "Thanks... I guess. Don't think this makes us friends.  The next time I see you, I'm still kicking your ass."

on_fail.message: You lunge for it. It does not want to be caught. It backhands you with what you can only describe as soap-slicked vengeance.

on_success.message: You decide this is not your problem and step over her, leaving her to fight the apparatus alone. Her muffled cursing follows you out.

rooms.prompt: You stop to catch your breath -- and notice you're not alone. A ragged group of hobos is huddled in the corner around a suspiciously well-organized dice game, using what you can only assume are stolen towels as a table cloth.

on_success.message: You flag down a bathhouse attendant and quietly point out the hobos. They slip you a little something for your trouble before hauling the group off, muttering about "freeloaders."

on_fail.message: The attendant squints at you, then at the huddled hobos, then back at you. "Wait... you're the one that's been causing trouble."

on_success.message: You buy in and snatch the dice before any hobo can do their hobo hexes on them.  You blow on them and throw them down.  Seven!  That's a winner!

on_fail.message: You buy in, but once the game starts the hobo's hands move so fast you can't even see what is happening.  Before you know it, you've lost.  You suspect the dice were never fair to begin with.

rooms.prompt: The bathhouse "staff", who look suspiciously like the gnomes you just flattened, surround you, absolutely certain you're the real troublemaker here.

name: Beneath the Buffet
flavor: Somewhere under a jungle-swallowed casino, the vault still waits.

rooms.prompt: Vines have swallowed the stone archway, but you can still make out gilded letters beneath the moss: THE KING'S CABANA. A door, propped open with a bar stool, leads down into the dark.

Roots as thick as a man's torso have broken through the tiled floor, pulsing faintly with a sickly green light. Something in here is very much alive, and it is not happy you're here. (placeholder room -- plant monsters TBD)

Ankle-deep water reflects a ceiling choked in hanging vines. Dozens of rotted crates, once labeled SWIZZLE STICKS -- DO NOT OPEN, have sprouted something with teeth. (placeholder room -- plant monsters TBD)

The tunnel behind you ruptures. A low, wet rumble builds into a roar, and the air fills with a smell like a tiki bar that's been closed for thirty years. Something enormous is barreling down the corridor, and it is very much a pineapple.

on_success.message: The party clears the straightaway with room to spare.

on_fail.message: It clips the stragglers on the way through.

rooms.prompt: The pineapple crashes through the wall ahead and wedges itself, spinning, into a massive roulette wheel embedded in the temple floor -- gilded, ancient, and somehow still perfectly balanced. It's still rolling. Somebody has to call it.

Past the wheel, the tunnel opens into a wide chamber -- and at its center, wreathed in thirty years of reclaiming vines, stands a carved tiki idol easily three times the height of a person. Its shipping tag still flutters from one wrist. As you approach, its carved grimace creaks... and turns to face you. (placeholder room -- The Big Kahuna mini-boss TBD)

A commercial kitchen, decades cold. The staff never actually left -- they're just still clocked in, spatulas in hand, eyes milk-white, technically still on shift. (placeholder room -- Zombie Staff TBD)
Cubicles stretch into the dark, every desk still occupied. A motivational poster reads TEAMWORK MAKES THE DREAM WORK in a font that is, somehow, also rotting. (placeholder room -- Zombie Staff TBD)
A wall of dead monitors flickers with security footage from a shift that ended a very long time ago. The guards are still watching. They never blinked. (placeholder room -- Zombie Staff TBD)
The heat down here never really left, and neither did whoever used to maintain it. Something big shifts in the dark between the pipes. (placeholder room -- tougher Zombie Staff TBD)

The vault door -- three feet of rusted steel -- hangs wide open. Sitting cross-legged on a mountain of chips, sequined jumpsuit somehow still gleaming under all this dust, is a figure who can only be described as Hellvis.

"Well, well. Look what crawled outta the buffet line." He snaps his fingers. Something enormous rises from the coins behind him. "Y'all have fun now." He's gone before the last coin stops spinning. (placeholder room -- this becomes the raid boss's summoned monster once designed)

name: Big Cheese Pizza Palace
flavor: Closed since the eighties, lit since the eighties, and somebody is still taking orders.

rooms.prompt:
The door is unlocked, the neon is on, and the smell hits you like a wall: thirty years of oregano and something underneath it that is not oregano.

A man in a paper hat and a grease-blackened apron looks up from a podium. "Evening. Do you have a reservation?"

There is a cup of brass tokens on the podium by his elbow. He has not blinked yet.

on_success.message: He talks for four uninterrupted minutes about a deal that expired in 1987. You help yourself to the token cup while he does it.

actions.label: Flash a coupon you definitely have

on_success.message: He studies the empty hand for a long moment, then stamps it anyway. "Right this way." He waves you past the dining room entirely, and tips the cup into your palm.

on_fail.message: "That's not a coupon. That's your hand." He rings the bell on the podium, and the dining room stands up.

on_success.message: The bills disappear into the apron. He unhooks the velvet rope and looks at the wall until you are past it.

rooms.prompt: Every booth is occupied and every head turns at once. Service here has never actually stopped.

A service window in the back wall, the kitchen dark behind it. A laminated sign, curled at every corner, offers the only two options this establishment has ever recognized.

Through the bead curtain to your left, something is playing an attract loop to an empty room.

on_success.message: A cup of tokens slides across the sill before you finish asking. The curtain rattles invitingly.
You skip the games and head for the back. Whatever's on the menu, you're picking it up yourself.

rooms.prompt:
Eleven cabinets, nine of them still lit, all of them still running. The carpet is that specific carpet. Behind the prize counter the good stuff sits exactly where a child could see it and never afford it.

Tokens in, tickets out, tickets across the counter. The house has not changed the rates in thirty years, and the house never needed to.

on_success.message: The last ball rattles into the 50 ring. The machine coughs up its paper without enthusiasm.

on_fail.message: Every ball goes straight up the middle for ten points. The machine does not even bother printing.

on_success.message: You clear the board before the last one is fully up. The machine plays a little fanfare it clearly means sincerely.

on_fail.message: One of them comes up under the mallet instead of over it, and it bites.

on_success.message: The puck goes up, the bell comes off its mount, and the machine pays out in something close to panic.

on_fail.message: The hammer rebounds harder than it struck. Your shoulder files a complaint.

on_success.message: The glass head swivels, considers you, and prints a fortune that is upsettingly specific. Tickets follow.

on_fail.message: The head swivels, considers you, and prints YOU WILL BE DISAPPOINTED SHORTLY. It was right.

on_success.message: The claw closes, actually HOLDS, and drops the prize down the chute. Somewhere a manager who has been dead for thirty years feels it.

on_fail.message: The claw brushes the pile, tightens on nothing, and rises with the dignity of a machine that has never once paid out.

actions.label: Prize counter: Succo Di Ratto (4 tickets)

on_success.message: Four tickets buys you the bottom shelf. The bottom shelf is rat juice.

actions.label: Prize counter: Greater Healing Draught (10 tickets)

on_success.message: Ten tickets, and the attendant who is not there slides you something that actually works.

actions.label: Prize counter: The Last Birthday Slice (25 tickets)

on_success.message: Twenty-five tickets. The slice comes off the top shelf still wearing somebody's name.
You pocket what's left and push through the bead curtain.

rooms.prompt: Paper hats on every chair, a cake thirty years past candles, and a banner reading HAPPY BIRTHDAY in letters that have gone brown. The party has been going the whole time and you are late.

The stage curtain pulls back on its original motor. Eight feet of mascot suit sits on a steel frame, and the cultists file in behind you to watch, hats on, hands folded.

The head comes up. The good eye finds you. Servos spin up somewhere in the chest.

It still thinks it has a show to do.

Past the stage, the walk-in door stands open on a room that is much larger than the building. The cult is already inside, kneeling in a ring, chanting an order into the dark.

Something at the center is most of the way finished. It is not finished yet.

You can end this now, while it is still only most of a thing. Or you can wait, and see what they have actually been cooking, and take whatever comes off the top.

on_success.message: You go through the ring before the chant finishes. The cult stops praying and starts working.
You stand at the edge of the ring and let them finish. The chant peaks. Somewhere, a bell dings.

rooms.prompt: The ring breaks apart into individual problems. Whatever was forming at the center sags, unfinished, and slides off the altar unformed. That leaves only the staff.

The chant stops all at once. Every cultist lies down flat.

The thing on the altar finishes, and keeps finishing, out past the walls of a walk-in freezer that is no longer a walk-in freezer. It is a pizza the width of the room and it is looking at you.

Your order is ready.

It comes apart the way a building comes apart, all at once and then in pieces, and the neon finally goes out.

The cultists are still lying flat. Nobody gets up. Somewhere back through the dark, an attract loop is still running on a cabinet that has not been told either.

The bell over the front door rings once behind you. Thirty years late, the Big Cheese Pizza Palace is closed.

on_success.message: You leave through the front, past the podium, past the empty token cup. Nobody asks if you have a reservation.
